title: Called by the Creator of All Things
summary: The one through whom and for whom all things were made has called us by name and made us heirs. Let that truth shape how we walk through today.
exhortation: I want to start with a question. How life-changing would it be if the richest man in the world called you up today and said, "I'm going to transfer all my wealth to you"? I think all of us would find that a pretty big deal. We'd probably go tell all our friends about it.
I want to compare that to when Jesus called us. How much bigger a deal is it that Jesus called us by name one day and said, "I'm going to transfer all my wealth to you"?

Hebrews 11:3 says, "By faith we understand that the universe was created by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible." John 1:3 says, "All things were made through him, and without him was not any thing made that was made." And Colossians 1:16 says, "For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities, all things were created through him and for him."

What an amazing thing that we have been called and adopted by the Creator of the universe: Jesus, through whom all things were created and for whom all things were created. He owns it all. He rules over it all. The universe, heaven and earth, are his. And he has called us by name.

Let us rejoice in that truth as we walk through this day. As things happen that are outside our control, the frustrating things and all the good things we receive, let's remember that we have been called and adopted through Jesus Christ, and that we are sons of the living God.
prayer: Lord, you have showered mercy upon mercy on undeserving people. Thank you for the mercy of forgiveness. Thank you, Jesus, that our sins are forgiven. It would have been totally just, and we would have been thrilled, simply to have our sins forgiven and to be your servants. But you showered us with your kindness. You brought us into your family. You made us co-heirs with Christ. What an astounding mercy.

So we thank you, Lord. We pray that we would live as sons and daughters of the King, purchased and redeemed at a great price. And may we practice praising and worshiping you with every breath, though it will never be enough. Lord, nothing brings more joy and satisfaction to our souls than returning praise to you for all your wondrous works and all your incredible deeds toward us. Thank you, Lord. In Jesus' name, amen.
